kind: diagnostic development blocks, not a census: the seeds below were used to find and fix the controllers' losses, so their rates are selected, not estimated
question: Why do the rebuild pilots lose on their hardest nights, and do the fixes named for each loss remove it?

explanationsTested.fnaf4: The warden's 57 losses in seeds 0-299 are (a) 53 near occupants never shut out, because the flash branch for Foxy far in the same hall came first and a flash with the occupant near returns at once, so the dwell ran to the black flash (g468); and (b) 4 walks to the bed with the Freddy counter at 60 or more (g427/g428), the bed having been blocked by a Chica dwell of 20 or more that survives her leaving the hall (g478) and clears only while her hall is viewed (g481).
explanationsTested.fnaf3: The guard's office losses are the audio economy: a play takes AI from `audio text` and needs it above -10 (g301/g308), so two plays per reboot at AI 7, one per 10.5 s (g299), and a lure fails one time in 7 (g317/g318); 30 of its 42 losses in seeds 1-53 entered stage 1 from CAM 02 or 03 with audio already at -10, and 8 were vent kills through 14 or 15 during a reboot. Under g252/g275 a marked stage 1 has no exit.

harness: tools/recompile/pilot/batch.mjs: native runtime, --stop-frame 5, --kill-on-loss, one seed per pilot; a seed WON only if the save the game wrote holds the win key. Seeds the harness can never start (FNaF 3's what-day rare screen under the per-visit seed, whatDayRare) are NO_NIGHT, not losses.
